subject: general
question: Why did Mendeleev leave gaps in his periodic table?

options.text: To make the table look symmetrical

solution:
The Correct answer is __**For undiscovered elements**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**, the Russian chemist, is credited with the creation of the first widely recognized periodic table.
 
• Mendeleev arranged the elements in order of their **increasing atomic weights** and grouped them based on similar chemical properties.
 
• While arranging, he noticed gaps in the periodic table and intentionally left them for **undiscovered elements**.
 
• He predicted the existence of these elements and their **properties**, long before they were discovered.
 
• Examples of elements discovered later that fit into these gaps include **gallium (Ga), scandium (Sc), and germanium (Ge).**
 
• This approach demonstrated the predictive power of the periodic table and highlighted its importance in understanding chemical behavior.
 
• The gaps ensured the periodic table remained organized and followed the **periodic law**, which states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic weights (later modified to atomic numbers).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To make the table look symmetrical**__

 __
 
• Mendeleev did not leave gaps for aesthetic purposes or symmetry; his focus was on the **scientific rationale** behind the arrangement of elements.
 
• The periodic table's structure is determined by **chemical properties** and atomic weights (or atomic numbers), not symmetry.
 
 
 
• **To include isotopes**__
 __
 
• Mendeleev's periodic table was based on **atomic weight**, not isotopes. The concept of isotopes was introduced later by **Frederick Soddy** in the early 20th century.
 
• Isotopes are variants of elements with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, and they were not part of Mendeleev's original table.
 
 
 
• **To avoid repetition of elements**__
 
 
• Mendeleev's periodic table did not have repetition of elements; each element had a unique place based on its **atomic weight** and chemical properties.
 
• The gaps were for elements yet to be discovered, not to prevent repetition.
